messages:
alyssa: Heads up — after the driver bump to 545.12 in staging we see a clear perf regression on long-context workloads (512/1024 seq). p50 is unchanged, but p95/p99 increased ~15–30%. KV-cache hit-rate dropped ~8% on those routes. Posting logs + quick flame: https://stash/reports/2178901234 :grimacing:

mike: Can you paste the numbers and affected model names? Is this only on H100?

alyssa: Quick numbers: model-redwood-7b-rlhf (fp16, q4) on h100s - p50 22ms -> 24ms, p95 78ms -> 98ms, p99 210ms -> 270ms. KV hit-rate 92% -> 84% on same traffic replay. Observed increased time in kernel launch + memcpy stalls in trace.

devon: Autotuner logs from the same run show the selector is choosing `fused-attn-v2` more often for seq<=768 after the driver change. It looks like the kernel preference score shifted because some microbench numbers changed post-driver. Late-binding heuristics picked the new kernel path more aggressively.

lisa: That matches the traces I saw — the new path has a higher setup overhead for small batches and hits a slow memcpy path on this driver. Two short options: rollback driver in staging, or force the selector to prefer `attn-v1` for these model+seqlen combos and run a canary.

ops-bot: Canary cluster: staging-uk (h100) — driver 545.12 rolled 02:14 UTC. Canary traffic: 100% staging, 0% prod. Deploys: green.

perf-bot: Perf snippet from harness (10k samples):
```
route: redwood-7b-rlhf
seq=512 batch=1
before(driver 544.xx): p95=78.2ms p99=209.8ms kv-hit=0.920
after(driver 545.12):  p95=98.3ms p99=269.5ms kv-hit=0.844
kernel-paths: attn-v1=32% fused-attn-v2=68% (after)
```

mike: We need a short playbook. Rollback driver has infra churn but is clean. Selector pin is lower blast radius. What's the risk of masking a real perf bug in fused-attn-v2?

devon: If fused-attn-v2 actually regressed on this driver, pinning will hide the root cause and delay proper fixes — but it's a good stopgap while we triage. We should capture microbench numbers across kernels with the exact driver lib to reproduce. I'll run the perf microbench matrix on 545.12 images.

alyssa: Proposed immediate actions (short):
1) Patch kernel-mapping config to prefer `attn-v1` for models: redwood-7b-rlhf, redwood-chat-7b; route 5% traffic to original mapping as canary. (owner: mike)
2) Start driver rollback plan for one canary hostpool if microbench repro confirms driver-induced slowdown. (owner: lisa)
3) Devon to run microbench matrix + collect autotuner logs and nvprof traces. (owner: devon)

mike: For (1) I'll open a lightweight change: `git revert` is overkill — we have dynamic kernel_map. I'll push config: `configs/kernel_map/2026-03-17-pin-attn-v1.yml` and route a 5% canary. Command I'll run: `rctl rollout kernel-map --route redwood-7b-rlhf --canary 5% --file=...`

devon: I'll spin up a small perf job: `bench/perf_matrix --driver=545.12 --models redwood-7b-rlhf,redwood-chat-7b --seqs 32,128,512,1024 --kernels attn-v1,fused-attn-v2` — will post results in ~45m. Also collecting `nvprof` traces for the 512 case.

lisa: I'll prepare rollback checklist in case we need to revert driver in staging: rollback script, test smoke, and notify SRE. If rollback is chosen we do one hostpool first (5 hosts), run synthetic load, validate KV-hit and p99.

alyssa: One more note — Optimize team, remember kv-cache prefetch thresholds are per-kernel; we should check whether the new kernel changed effective prefix handling which reduced cache reuse. If so, the fix might be kernel-side or heuristic.

mike: Agree. Immediate: I will push the kernel_map pin and start the 5% canary. If canary metrics improve, keep it for 24h while devon finishes repro. If not, we'll escalate to rollback.

devon: Started jobs. I see the microbench already showing 20% slower latency for fused-attn-v2 on 512 sequence in the 545.12 image. Will paste raw numbers soon.

lisa: Noted. I'll stand by for rollback window and coordinates. Tagging @oncall-sre once we decide to rollback: :bell: 

alyssa: Thanks team. Keep updates to this thread. If anyone notices prod anomalies, raise immediately. :thumbsup:
